topic: Understanding Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Intuition: Same Reality, Different Maps
lecture_lines: A vector is a physical reality.
Different bases describe the same vector.
We use grids as our frame.
animations: Create two coordinate systems using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg], System A (#FF0000) and System B (#00FF00), showing the same [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg].
Move [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] in System A, observe coordinate changes in B.
Highlight [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] invariance across systems using a bold white circle.
Display the transformation equation: VectorB = M * VectorA.
Fade out [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] labels while keeping [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] and equation.

sections.title: Defining the Transformation Matrix
animations: Define basis vectors i and j for System A (#FF0000).
Show how i and j map to new positions in B.
Construct a 2x2 grid representing Matrix M with color coding. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg]
Show column vectors of M as transformed basis vectors.
Pulse Matrix M to emphasize its role as a bridge.
